fml.menu.mods.info.description.headinaja: Take your head off and live in a life-support jar: drive your own headless body over a neuro-link, borrow mob bodies, build mecha, splice genes and put jarred heads to work.
jei.headinajar.separation_chair: Load a Life Support Jar, Relay Goggles, a Collar Cam and four Cranial Saline, and store 40 kFE in it from a Galvanic Pile or Leyden Jar touching it. Sit down and hold Sign on Form 27-B: it takes your head off and leaves your body linked to it. Sneak and use it to open its panel without sitting.
jei.headinajar.life_support_cradle: Holds your head while you walk your body, and a docked head uses no saline. Each second the Cradle refills your saline from its tank, moves up to 10 kFE into your charge and uses 100 FE; every 10 seconds it mends a point of glass. It does not extend the link.
jei.headinajar.saline_mixer: 1,000 mB of water, a sugar, a kelp and a redstone, with 2,000 FE over 10 seconds, make 1,000 mB of Cranial Saline. Water goes in by bucket or pipe. Glass bottles in its slot are filled at 250 mB each; an empty bucket takes a bucketful.
jei.headinajar.body_printer: Prints a new headless body for a head in a jar, in 60 seconds: 16 rotten flesh, 8 bone blocks, 4 redstone blocks, 8 slime balls, 2,000 mB of saline and 200 kFE. With a DNA Fraction of quality 40 or better in the Template slot it prints a host of that species instead, materials scaled by its size; anyone may press Print.
jei.headinajar.surgical_saw: Use on a creature at half its health or less: its body becomes a host. With an empty jar in the other hand you keep its head; slimes, bees, vexes and other creatures that are mostly head need one, and big heads need a Reinforced or Executive jar. Babies, bosses, named creatures, other people's pets and hosts are refused, and a refusal costs nothing.
jei.headinajar.assembly_gantry: Put a frame and modules in, then Assemble (10,000 FE). Take Apart pulls a mecha back into the slots; Repair spends Mecha Plating.
jei.headinajar.centrifuge: Spins a Blood Sample into a DNA Fraction and a Plasma Vial. Dragon's breath gives Ender Dragon DNA.
jei.headinajar.dna_sequencer: Reads a DNA Fraction into your gene library, a share at a time. Auto takes 10 s at 60% accuracy; calling the twelve bases yourself is instant, 50 to 100% by how many you get right. Each read costs 4,000 FE.
jei.headinajar.gene_splicer: Splices up to three library genes (at least 30% read) into a Serum Cassette with Bio-Gel, a glass bottle and an optional catalyst. Each row's chip picks a department, its arrows a gene of it.
jei.headinajar.injection_rig: Injects the serum in its slot into your own body (with your head on, or linked).
jei.headinajar.leech_jar: Takes a small blood sample every 30 s from a creature standing next to it.
jei.headinajar.syringe: Use on a living creature to draw a Blood Sample. Healthier creatures give better quality.
jei.headinajar.serum_cassette: Made at the Gene Splicer. Use it on a host or on a mecha with a Gene Port, or load it into an Injection Rig.
jei.headinajar.turret_pedestal: Fit a Jarred Head: it guards 16 blocks around the way that mob fights. Skeleton, Stray and Bogged heads need arrows in a chest below or beside it. Power: 1 FE/t on watch, 10 FE/t with a target.
jei.headinajar.cerebral_array: Up to nine jarred heads make FE from Nutrient Broth. Five or more hold a Board Meeting (+10%).
jei.headinajar.employee_mount: Hang a jarred villager on a machine: their profession gives that machine a bonus, for an emerald a day.
jei.headinajar.neural_socket: Plug your jar in to drive six redstone channels, or let a mob head run a program.
jei.headinajar.entangled_pair: Use it to split it into two shards. Craft one with your goggles and the other with your Collar Cam: the link then crosses dimensions.
jei.headinajar.emp_grenade: Throw it: links break (unless shielded), jars and mecha lose power, turrets go dark.
jei.headinajar.jarred_head: A mob's head in a jar, from the Surgical Saw with an empty jar in your off hand. A placed villager keeps trading. Heads work in Turret Pedestals, the Cerebral Array and Neural Sockets; villagers also on an Employee Mount.
jei.headinajar.frame: Assemble it at the Assembly Gantry with modules in the slots of the right kind.

book.headinajar.written.1:
Noggin & Sons
EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK

The opening chapters.

The full handbook, with every department, comes with the Patchouli mod. Lost this copy? A book and a Surgical Steel Blend make another.
book.headinajar.written.2:
WELCOME

Congratulations on joining Head Office. This handbook covers what an employee needs, from the Separation Chair to keeping your head topped up with Cranial Saline.
book.headinajar.written.3: Start with Surgical Steel: smelt a blend of iron, bone meal and coal. Then make Neuro-Copper Wire, a Lens and a Servo. Power comes from a Galvanic Pile fed with meat or rotten flesh.
book.headinajar.written.4:
THE SEPARATION CHAIR

Load the chair with a Life Support Jar, Relay Goggles, a Collar Cam and four bottles of Cranial Saline, and give it 40 kFE. Sit down and hold Sign on Form 27-B.
book.headinajar.written.5: You may get up until the cut. After that, DOLORES will finish what she started. A worn blade can botch the job: keep a Replacement Blade handy.
book.headinajar.written.6:
THE NEURO-LINK

After the cut you walk around in your own headless body and see through the Collar Cam. Your head wears the goggles and sends the signal. The further apart they are, the worse the picture.
book.headinajar.written.7: Water, rock, storms, portals and the Warden all hurt the signal. At zero for five seconds you wake up in your head. Press %s to swap between body and head yourself.
book.headinajar.written.8: Carry your head in a Head Satchel for a perfect link, or dock it in a Life Support Cradle. Relay Masts pass the signal along: masts reach each other and your body within their radius.
book.headinajar.written.9:
WHEN IT GOES WRONG

If your body dies, it becomes a corpse that keeps your things, and you wake up in your head. As a jar, use a Suture Kit on the corpse to get back into it, or print a new body.
book.headinajar.written.10: If your head is destroyed while you are out walking, that is a real death. Guard it. A Signal Jammer near your enemies works wonders.
book.headinajar.written.11:
GETTING HOME

Walk too far and the link breaks: you wake up in your head. A jar with the Wheels module drives at half walking speed: press %s. Without wheels the same key tips the jar on its side to roll, very slowly.
book.headinajar.written.12: Stranded anyway? Press Courier in the jar menu. A Noggin & Sons courier delivers your body to your head in 30 seconds, from anywhere, for 20 kFE of charge (or all you have, if less). Then press %s.

gene.headinajar.ruminant_gut.desc: Food fills a quarter more. Sneak and use grass, empty-handed, to graze. Wheat is lunch. A host on grass holds off rot.
gene.headinajar.stew_glands.desc: Small flowers are food, with their stew effect, most for three times as long. Sneak and use a bowl: stew, every 5 min.
gene.headinajar.stew_glands.cost: Cost: stews fill half, and a wither rose withers you.
gene.headinajar.swine_appetite.desc: Rotten flesh, spider eyes, raw chicken, poisonous potatoes and pufferfish never make you sick. Rotten flesh fills 2 more.
gene.headinajar.swine_appetite.cost: Cost: you oink at every bite.
gene.headinajar.fleece.desc: You grow a fleece in 5 min. Fleeced, your steps, landings and meals make no vibrations, and powder snow cannot freeze you.
gene.headinajar.fleece.cost: Cost: fleeced, fire burns longer and 25% harder.
gene.headinajar.mountain_hooves.desc: You walk up full blocks (not while sneaking), falls of up to 7 blocks do not hurt, and you walk on powder snow.
gene.headinajar.phase.desc: Active: dash 5 blocks along your look, through up to 2 blocks of wall, into open space. 6 s cooldown. Claims hold.
gene.headinajar.phase.cost: Cost: each phase takes 2 health from a host, 3% from a mecha.
gene.headinajar.bamboo_diet.desc: Bamboo and sugar cane are food, eaten at once. Cake slices fill double.
gene.headinajar.bamboo_diet.cost: Cost: you sit down to eat.
gene.headinajar.snow_pounce.desc: Active: leap to the block you look at within 8. Creatures where you land take 3, are knocked back and slowed. 4 s cooldown.
gene.headinajar.snow_pounce.cost: Cost: by day under open sky, the cooldown is 8 s.
gene.headinajar.pollinator.desc: Crops and saplings you pass get a growth tick, each once a minute at most. Bees never anger at you. Honey fills 4 more.
gene.headinajar.arctic_coat.desc: You never freeze. Slowness on you lasts half as long. You swim 30% faster.
gene.headinajar.arctic_coat.cost: Cost: heat and the Nether slow you and make you hungry.
gene.headinajar.roll_up.desc: Sneak still for a second and you curl up low: 60% less damage and no knockback. You shed a scute every 20 minutes.
gene.headinajar.roll_up.cost: Cost: curled, you cannot move, hit or use anything.
gene.headinajar.keen_nose.desc: Creatures whose gene you have not finished reading leave a scent only you see. Suspicious sand puffs. Sneak on grass for seeds.
gene.headinajar.mimicry.desc: Every 8 s, you imitate a hostile within 32 blocks that you cannot see. Out loud. A creeper's hiss, from behind the wall.
gene.headinajar.tongue.desc: Active: lick what you look at within 8. Items and creatures up to chicken size come to you; a small slime is eaten. 2 s cooldown.
gene.headinajar.tongue.cost: Cost: you croak when you jump.
gene.headinajar.tadpole_tail.cost: Cost: none. It is a tadpole.
gene.headinajar.puffer.desc: A hostile within 2, or a melee hit, puffs you up for 3 s: 30% bigger, and what touches you is poisoned. Pufferfish is safe to eat.
gene.headinajar.puffer.cost: Cost: puffed, you are 30% slower and cannot sprint.
gene.headinajar.spit_gland.desc: Active: spit at what you look at within 12: 1 damage, and a creature loses interest in you for 4 s, once in 12 s. 2 s cooldown.
gene.headinajar.spit_gland.cost: Cost: stand in front of you for 5 s and get spat at.
gene.headinajar.dusk_draught.desc: At dusk you turn invisible for 60 s. At night, the first hostile to target you in 2 min makes you vanish for 8 s.
gene.headinajar.dusk_draught.cost: Cost: at dawn you drink any milk you carry: every effect goes.
gene.headinajar.undeath.desc: Harming heals you and Healing harms. Poison and Regeneration do nothing. Zombies, husks and drowned ignore you till you hit one.
gene.headinajar.undeath.cost: Cost: bare-headed, daylight burns you. Smite hurts.
gene.headinajar.sun_baked.desc: Daylight never burns you, Undeath or no Undeath. Your melee hits leave players hungry and creatures weakened.
gene.headinajar.sun_baked.cost: Cost: 30 s in water slows you for a minute.
gene.headinajar.rehabilitated.desc: Villagers give you the cured-zombie discount, as if you had cured them yourself.
gene.headinajar.rehabilitated.cost: Cost: golden apples sicken you. Hit a villager: suspended a day.
gene.headinajar.gilded_rot.desc: Golden swords and axes do 3 more to the undead and lose no durability on them. A zombified piglin you hit fights you alone.
gene.headinajar.gilded_rot.cost: Cost: gold armour wears out twice as fast.
gene.headinajar.rampage.desc: Each melee hit within 3 s of the last does 1 more, up to 3 more. Three quiet seconds end the streak.
gene.headinajar.rampage.cost: Cost: on a streak you take 15% more damage and cannot sneak.
gene.headinajar.bowstring_arms.desc: A bow draws fully in 0.7 s instead of 1, and your arrows do 1 more.
gene.headinajar.rime_arrows.desc: Your arrows, from a bow or a crossbow, slow what they hit for 5 s.
gene.headinajar.spore_arrows.desc: Your arrows, from a bow or a crossbow, poison what they hit for 4 s.
gene.headinajar.spore_arrows.cost: Cost: poison on you lasts 50% longer.
gene.headinajar.undertow_stride.desc: You walk the seabed at land speed, jump off it and do not float.
gene.headinajar.undertow_stride.cost: Cost: you sink, and swim up half as fast.
gene.headinajar.snow_trail.desc: You leave snow where you walk, wherever a snow golem would. Your snowballs do 2 and slow for 2 s.
gene.headinajar.snow_trail.cost: Cost: you melt in hot places, the Nether and the rain.
gene.headinajar.gold_standard.desc: Piglins treat you as if you wore gold. Golden carrots and golden apples give half as much again.
gene.headinajar.gold_standard.cost: Cost: gold in sight on the ground slows you 10%.
gene.headinajar.brute_strength.desc: Axes do 3 more, and Weakness does nothing to you.
gene.headinajar.brute_strength.cost: Cost: piglins attack you, gold or no gold, and never barter.
gene.headinajar.breaking_and_entering.de: With an axe, wooden doors, trapdoors and fence gates break in one hit and drop. Axes do 1 more. Claims hold.
gene.headinajar.breaking_and_entering.co: Cost: villagers will not trade while you hold an axe.
gene.headinajar.steady_aim.desc: Crossbows load 40% faster. Bolts fly 25% faster, and so hit about a quarter harder.
gene.headinajar.fang_line.desc: Active: a line of eight evoker fangs toward your aim within 12, 6 to each creature caught. Look down for a ring. 4 s cooldown.
gene.headinajar.fang_line.cost: Cost: blue sheep nearby turn red. Mecha: 15% of its heat limit.
gene.headinajar.potion_tolerance.desc: Potions you drink last 50% longer. Harmful potions splashed on you last half as long.
gene.headinajar.potion_tolerance.cost: Cost: milk does nothing for you.
gene.headinajar.bulldoze.desc: Leaves, crops, saplings, bamboo, vines, flowers, sugar cane and cobwebs break as you walk into them. Claims hold.
gene.headinajar.bulldoze.cost: Cost: you trample everything, your own farm included.
gene.headinajar.weeping_glands.desc: A Ghast Tear every 20 minutes: at a host's feet, or into a mecha's Cargo Hold.
gene.headinajar.weeping_glands.cost: Cost: it sobs every few minutes, and fogs a mecha's glass.
gene.headinajar.pearl_digestion.desc: An ender pearl you throw flies half as far again, does you no harm, and its cooldown is halved.
gene.headinajar.pearl_digestion.cost: Cost: endermen attack you on sight.
gene.headinajar.levitation_bolt.desc: Active: a homing shulker bullet at what you aim at within 24: 4 damage and 3 s of Levitation. 3 s cooldown.
gene.headinajar.levitation_bolt.cost: Cost: a mecha takes 10% of its heat limit a shot.

gene.headinajar.stone_lungs.cost: Cost: one stone block in a hundred lets out a silverfish.

memo.headinajar.no_hands: You are a jar now, and jars have no hands. The company’s own machines answer you; nothing else will. Fit a %2$s from the jar menu (%1$s): craft it with your hands on (3 iron ingots, redstone, a copper ingot) and keep it in your pocket.

jei.headinajar.galvanic_pile: Burns fuel into 20 FE/t and gives it to the machines touching it. Rotten flesh gives 4,000 FE, a spider eye 6,000 and raw meat or fish 3,000. Use fuel on it, or put it in with a hopper.
jei.headinajar.leyden_jar: Stores 250 kFE. It fills from a power source beside it and feeds its other neighbours at up to 2,000 FE/t. Two Leyden Jars do not feed each other.
jei.headinajar.tesla_node: Sends up to 2,000 FE/t to a linked node up to 16 blocks away, losing 5%. Link two with a Surgical Wrench, the sending node first. The receiving node feeds the machines touching it.
jei.headinajar.surgical_wrench: Links Tesla Nodes: use the sending node, then the receiving one. Sneak and use the sending node to unlink it.
jei.headinajar.charging_dock: Charges a jar standing on it at up to 500 FE/t from the 20 kFE it holds. Your head, set down on it while you walk your body, charges too. Feed it from a Galvanic Pile, a Leyden Jar or a cable.
jei.headinajar.replacement_blade: Use it on the Separation Chair while it is idle: blade wear goes back to 0. A blade over 80% worn can botch a cut.
jei.headinajar.glass_patch: Mends 5 points of Jar Integrity. Use it on your placed head, or put it in the jar menu's feed slot.
jei.headinajar.saline_bottle: Keeps a head alive: 250 mB a bottle. Use it on your placed head, or put it in the jar menu's feed slot. The Separation Chair takes four.
jei.headinajar.cranial_saline_bucket: 1,000 mB of Cranial Saline, taken from a Saline Mixer with an empty bucket. It fills a Life Support Cradle or a Body Printer.
jei.headinajar.life_support_jar: Load it into the Separation Chair: your head lives in it. 3 module slots, 100 kFE of charge, 1,000 mB of saline and 10 points of glass.
jei.headinajar.compact_life_support_jar: The same as a Life Support Jar, head-sized: your head faces the front and the whole jar turns with it. Craft either kind alone to get the other.
jei.headinajar.reinforced_life_support_j: 5 module slots, 250 kFE of charge, 1,500 mB of saline and 20 points of glass. Load it into the Separation Chair instead of a plain jar.
jei.headinajar.executive_life_support_ja: 7 module slots, 500 kFE of charge, 2,000 mB of saline and 30 points of glass. Load it into the Separation Chair instead of a plain jar.
jei.headinajar.manipulator_arm: A jar module. Without it a jar cannot mine, place, fight, use items or pick things up. Each block broken or placed and each hit costs 200 FE of charge.
jei.headinajar.relay_mast: Passes the neuro-link on: from your head within goggle range, to other masts and to your body within 96 blocks. Each mast costs 3% of the signal. Needs 1 FE a tick from a powered neighbour.
jei.headinajar.relay_mast_mk2: A Relay Mast with a 192-block radius. The same 1 FE a tick.
jei.headinajar.signal_jammer: Cuts the neuro-link of anyone within 16 blocks to 30%, except its owner and the players they trust. Needs 4 FE a tick.
jei.headinajar.body_locker: Use it to store the nearest host body within 3 blocks; nothing rots inside. Use it again to let it out in front. Takes robot shells and your own mecha too.
jei.headinajar.safety_placard: Hangs on a wall. Use it to change the notice: there are nineteen.
jei.headinajar.neural_lace: Use it on a host body at 50% sync or more: it never rots again.
jei.headinajar.embalming_fluid: Use it on a host body: fresh again, and it rots at half speed for a day.
jei.headinajar.board_room_core: Goes in the Cerebral Array's tenth slot. It lets one Dragon Head sit in the Array, making 300 FE/t.
jei.headinajar.quantum_knot: A part. It goes into the Entangled Pair and the Quantum Goggles.
jei.headinajar.plasma_vial: Comes out of the Centrifuge with each DNA Fraction. It makes Bio-Gel and Gene Wash, and fuels a mecha's Bio-Reactor Core from the Cargo Hold.
jei.headinajar.precision_syringe: Draws Blood Samples of quality 60 to 90, without hurting the creature. Bosses still need a Leviathan Needle.
jei.headinajar.lunk_chassis: Place it, then use it as a jar to climb in. A strong, slow robot body with 60 HP that tosses what it looks at. Runs on the jar's charge.
jei.headinajar.rover_chassis: Place it, then use it as a jar to climb in. A fast robot body; sneak-use it to open its 9-slot hold. Runs on the jar's charge.
jei.headinajar.spider_walker_chassis: Place it, then use it as a jar to climb in. A robot body that climbs walls, takes no fall damage and shoots webs. Runs on the jar's charge.
jei.headinajar.body_recall_beacon: A jar module. While you are a jar, your standing body walks to you, 10 FE a tick, in the same dimension and a loaded chunk. It stops at lava, fire and big drops.
jei.headinajar.suture_kit: Puts your head back on. Carrying your own head, hold use for 3 seconds; as a jar, use it on your body or corpse. Modules and an empty jar come back.
jei.headinajar.treadmill: A host walks on it in place and makes 4 to 24 FE/t by species; it stores 10 kFE and pushes up to 1,000 FE/t from its near end. Ride a host on and get off to clock it in.
jei.headinajar.staff_lanyard: Use it on a living creature to hire it. Hostiles at half their health or less.
jei.headinajar.time_clock: Makes a site 16 blocks out: staff punch in, take Job Cards and are paid at dawn from its drawer.
jei.headinajar.clipboard: Binds to a Time Clock, marks Pick-Ups, Drop-Offs and areas, and prints Job Cards on paper.
jei.headinajar.secondment_collar: Fits round a host's neck; a jarred head seated on it drives the body and works your sites.

book.headinajar.written2.orientation.wel:
Welcome to Head Office. Noggin & Sons takes your head off, keeps it alive in a jar and lets your body walk on without it.

This handbook is issued on your first day. Lost it? A book and a Surgical Steel Blend make another.

• Smelt Surgical Steel.
• Build a Galvanic Pile; fuel it.
• Make 4 Cranial Saline.
• Build and load the Separation Chair.
• Sit, sign, collect your head.

The Shopping List says what to bring.
book.headinajar.written2.orientation.sho: One operation, satchel included: 29 iron, 24 bone meal, 24 coal, 14 copper, 21 redstone, 19 glass, 4 amethyst shards, 8 leather, 2 string, 3 white wool, 1 slime ball, 2 kelp, 2 sugar, 11 rotten flesh, wood and stone.

Far from home:
• amethyst: a geode
• slime ball: a swamp
• kelp: the sea

No Nether trip is needed. Ten of the rotten flesh are fuel for the chair's 40 kFE.

24 ingots, each one Blend: iron, bone meal, coal.

DOLORES notes: receipts in triplicate.
book.headinajar.written2.orientation.how:
Keys show as you bound them: the jar menu is %1$s.

JEI shows recipes; Jade reads bodies, hosts and mecha. Use a pile or power block empty-handed to see its charge.

Advancements are your to-do list.

Two controls on one key? Another mod may share it: the key shows in red on the Options, Controls screen. Rebind one of the two there. The ability key and sprint may share a key on purpose; the game says so the first time.
book.headinajar.written2.orientation.uni:
FE: energy.
kFE: 1,000 FE.
FE/t: FE per tick; 20 ticks make a second.
mB: a thousandth of a bucket. A bottle of saline is 250 mB.

All times are real time.

DOLORES notes: one head per employee.
book.headinajar.written2.facilities.galv: The first generator: 20 FE/t, stores 50 kFE.

Use fuel on it, or hopper it in. FE per item:
• rotten flesh 4,000
• spider eye 6,000
• raw meat or fish 3,000

Cooked food will not burn. It powers any machine touching it: 10 rotten flesh give the chair its 40 kFE in 100 s.
book.headinajar.written2.facilities.shar: Power flows from a Galvanic Pile, Leyden Jar or Tesla Node into every machine touching any face, shared evenly. Machines do not pass it on: put the source against the machine. FE cables from other mods work too.

A Leyden Jar stores 250 kFE. It fills from a source beside it and feeds its other neighbours, 2,000 FE/t; two do not feed each other.

A Tesla Node sends up to 2,000 FE/t to a node within 16 blocks, losing 5%%.

To link two nodes, hold a Surgical Wrench: use the sending node, then the receiving one. Sneak and use the sender to unlink.

The source goes against the sender; the receiver feeds what touches it.
book.headinajar.written2.facilities.char: Charges a jar standing on it, 500 FE/t, from the 20 kFE it holds.

In your body, set your head on it from the Head Satchel: it charges there too.

Feed it from a source beside it. A pile alone gives 20 FE/t; a Leyden Jar keeps it stocked.

DOLORES notes: wipe your jar first.
book.headinajar.written2.life_support.sa: Made by hand, two bottles of 250 mB each. The chair wants four.

A jar holds 1,000 mB. Your head uses 1 mB per 12 s while you are the jar or it is set down: 3 h 20 min a full jar. In the Head Satchel or a Cradle, none.

Top up: use a bottle on your placed head, or the jar menu's feed slot.

The Saline Mixer: 1,000 mB of water, a sugar, a kelp, a redstone and 2,000 FE make 1,000 mB in 10 s. Water by bucket or pipe.

It fills glass bottles in its slot. An empty bucket takes a bucketful, for Cradle and Printer.
book.headinajar.written2.life_support.in:
Integrity is the glass: 10 points. As the jar, damage takes glass first, then health. A placed head is only glass: at 0 it breaks. Players cannot harm it; fire and lava crack a point a second.
No saline: a point lost per 30 s.
Mends 5 points: use it on your placed head, or the feed slot.
book.headinajar.written2.life_support.cr: A head in it uses no saline. It does not extend the link. Fill it by bottle or bucket.

Each second it refills a docked head's saline, moves up to 10 kFE of charge and uses 100 FE; every 10 s it mends a point of glass.
To dock, use it with your head in the Head Satchel; again to take it out. As the jar: use it, then Swap.
book.headinajar.written2.life_support.bo: A new body, Collar Cam fitted, in 60 s, for 16 rotten flesh, 8 bone blocks, 4 redstone blocks, 8 slime balls, 2,000 mB of saline and 200 kFE stored first.

Load it before you need it: when you do, you are a jar and your things are on your corpse. Saline goes in by bucket or bottle. From a pile alone, 200 kFE take over 8 min.

Then, as the jar, press Print. Use the new body, or Swap, to step in.

Print-to-Order: a DNA Fraction of quality 40 or better in the Template slot prints a headless host of its species, in 60 s, at the fraction's quality as freshness. Anyone may press Print; the presser is its employer. The fraction is used up. Printed hosts drop no loot when they die.

The door is one block wide, two tall. Tiny (chicken, rabbit, frog, fish): a quarter of the materials. Small (pig, sheep, wolf, fox, cat): half. Medium (cow, villager, zombie, creeper, strider, llama, squid): a full print. Marine models need water at the doorstep. No bosses, golems, spirits or heads alone.
book.headinajar.written2.separation.the_: The tray slides out to its left. Keep that side, the front and the top clear.

• a Life Support Jar
• Relay Goggles
• a Collar Cam
• 4 Cranial Saline
• 40 kFE, from a pile or Leyden Jar touching it

Load them in its panel; sneak and use the chair to open it without sitting.

Use it to sit; hold Sign for 2 s. It takes 12 s; in the first 5 you may get up, keeping the parts, losing 10 kFE.

Your head goes on the tray (or an empty Cradle within 3 blocks). To carry it, use it with a Head Satchel in your inventory.
Range 48 blocks; Mk II 160, Mk III 640. Use new ones on your placed or docked head.
Bolted to your neck: your body sees through it.

Incident 0017: Oopsie

Each operation adds 5%% blade wear. Over 80%%, a cut may botch: 10%% at 85, 40%% at 100.
A botch flips your view for 30 s and bends the Collar Cam: -10%% range, for good.

Resets an idle chair's wear to 0.

DOLORES notes: so shiny.

Linked, you walk your body and see through the Collar Cam. The bar shows LINK %%, delay, which end you are and the distance.

Signal is full to half the goggles' range, 0 at the range. Your head in the Head Satchel gives 100%%.

Water, deep rock, thunder, portals and Darkness weaken it. Under 20%%, clicks get lost; 5 s at 0%% and you wake in your head.

The swap key, %1$s, takes your body to head always, but head to body only over 20%%.
book.headinajar.written2.separation.when:
FROM: DOLORES
TO: All Staff
RE: Drying Out

Out of saline, a placed head loses 1 glass per 30 s; at 0 glass it is a real death. A full jar lasts 3 h 20 min, then 5 min of warnings.

Not a death: losing the link, or your body dying (a corpse keeps your things).

Real death: your placed head breaking or drying while you walk, or dying as the jar. Modules drop; you respawn with a head.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.no_hands.1:
FROM: DOLORES
TO: All Staff
RE: Hands

Without a Manipulator Arm a jar cannot mine, place, fight, use items or pick things up. Doors and chests do not answer.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.no_hands.2:
A bare jar can still:
• use every Noggin & Sons machine
• step back into its own body
• board a boat or minecart
• ride a host
• use its keys and modules
• pick up with a Magnet
book.headinajar.written2.jar.no_hands.3: Hands: half speed, half damage, 200 FE a block or hit.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.jar_menu.1: As the jar, press %1$s. Modules go in the top row, one of each. The feed slot takes redstone, saline and Glass Patches.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.modules.1:
Moving
• Hop Springs: 60%% speed, 100 FE a hop
• Spider Legs: 80%%, steps up
• Suction Cups: climb walls
• Propeller: fly, 25 FE/t
• Water Jet: swim, 50 FE/t
book.headinajar.written2.jar.modules.2:
Wheels: %1$s drops them; half speed, 10 FE/t moving.

Without Wheels the same key tips the jar on its side to roll, very slowly, for free.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.modules.3:
Reach
• Drill Bit: the arm mines 6x faster
• Magnet: pulls items in 6 blocks
• Telekinesis Module: %1$s grabs (500 FE) and holds (50 FE/t); attack throws (2,000 FE). No arm needed.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.modules.4:
Defence
• Armour Plating: +6 armour
• Heat Shield: no fire harm, 100 FE/t
• Shock Lid: zaps hitters, 500 FE
• Self-Righting Gyro: no knockback
• Lacrimal Laser: %1$s, 4 damage, 1,500 FE
book.headinajar.written2.jar.modules.5:
Upkeep
• Hub Antenna: +50%% range
• Saline Recycler: half saline
• Body Recall Beacon: body walks to you, 10 FE/t
• Life Sign Monitor: body's health

The rest: see the tooltips.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.charge.1:
A jar holds 100 kFE, full from the chair. As the jar you spend 2 FE/t: about 40 min. In your body, nothing.
At 0 powered modules stop; Armour Plating, Drill Bit, Magnet, Self-Righting Gyro and Night Lens still work.
book.headinajar.written2.jar.charge.2:
To recharge:
• feed slot: redstone, 5 kFE a dust, 45 a block
• Charging Dock: stand on it, 500 FE/t
• a Dock under your placed head
• a Cradle holding your head: up to 10 kFE a second
book.headinajar.written2.jar.tiers.1:
• Basic: 3 slots, 100 kFE, 1,000 mB, 10 glass
• Compact: as Basic, head-sized
• Reinforced: 5 slots, 250 kFE, 1,500 mB, 20 glass
• Executive: 7 slots, 500 kFE, 2,000 mB, 30 glass
The chair takes any.
book.headinajar.written2.getting_home.re: Goggles reach 48 blocks (Mk I), 160 (Mk II), 640 (Mk III) or the whole dimension (Quantum). Signal is full to half the range, gone at the edge; near another's powered Signal Jammer (16 blocks), 30%%. Going back into your body needs over 20%%.
A powered mast passes the link on: head to mast in goggle range, then mast to mast and on to the body within 96 blocks (192 for Mk II). Each mast costs 3%%. It draws 1 FE/t.
book.headinajar.written2.getting_home.co: Stranded as a jar? Press Courier in the jar menu, or type /headoffice courier. In 30 s your body, or its corpse, arrives beside you from anywhere, for 20 kFE (or all your charge). Step into a body with %1$s; a corpse takes a Suture Kit.
A jar module: while you are a jar, your standing body walks to you, 10 FE/t. Same dimension and loaded chunks only. It halts before lava, fire or a drop of over 3 blocks.
book.headinajar.written2.getting_home.su: With a Suture Kit: carrying your own head, hold %1$s for 3 s; or, as a jar, use it on your body or corpse. You stand up whole and dizzy. Modules and an empty jar come back, goggles and collar a little worn; a corpse gives your things back.
book.headinajar.written2.getting_home.co: A linked body that dies becomes a corpse with your armour and inventory, and you wake up in your head. Nothing hurts a corpse. Only you, and those you trust (/headoffice trust add), may use it to open it.

Incident 0119: No Suture Kit

As the jar, use the corpse. A Suture Kit on you or among its things is used at once. With no kit, the corpse opens its inventory so you can craft one. No body at all: the Body Printer.
book.headinajar.written2.getting_home.lo: Type /headoffice status. It prints your form, your link, where your head is (in you, set down, docked or in the satchel) and where your body is (standing or a corpse), each with dimension and coordinates, and your charge.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.saw.1: Use it on a creature at half its health or less: the body stays up as a host. With a jar in your off hand, you keep the head.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.saw.2:
Who Gives What
Any jar takes a head, and the body falls.
Head only, in a jar, which takes all of it: slime, magma cube, shulker, vex, bee, silverfish, endermite, tadpole.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.saw.3: Big heads: a Reinforced Life Support Jar or bigger for a warden, elder guardian, hoglin, zoglin, sniffer or medium slime; an Executive one for a ghast, ravager or big slime.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.saw.4:
Neither: the Dragon, the Wither, other bosses, babies, named creatures, other people's pets, hosts, armour stands.
A refused cut costs nothing: no jar, no wear.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.saw.5:
Snow golem: the first cut takes its pumpkin off. Saw again for the head.

Babies: come back when it is grown. A server may allow them.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.riding: As a jar, use a host to ride it. Linked and carrying your head, use it too: your body stays standing and the jar climbs on. The host goes where you look; fliers rise while you hold %1$s. %2$s attacks as the host does; %3$s dismounts.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.sync.1: Sync grows 5%% a minute while you ride; on the first climb, each ring you hit adds 3%%. A body moves its own way from the first second: a flier flies, a spider climbs, a chicken floats. At 25%% its other traits work.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.sync.2:
At 50%% %1$s fires its ability, at 75%% %2$s the second (blaze, enderman, ravager and the five of Every Body Does Something). At 100%%: 10%% stronger.

A seconded head earns team sync at work instead; it counts for the lace.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.abilit:
Host Abilities
What %1$s does in each host, from 50%% sync:
Sprint: horse, donkey, mule, ocelot
Charge: camel, dolphin, goat, ravager
Pounce: wolf, fox, phantom

Web: spiders
Arrows: skeleton, stray
Fireballs: blaze, ghast
Teleport: enderman
Explode: creeper (halves your glass)
Call their kind: zombie, husk, drowned
Toss: iron golem

Roar: polar bear
Ink: squids
Echolocation: bat
Wind charge: breeze
Egg: chicken
Potion: witch
Sonic boom: warden

The rest: Every Body Does Something.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.upkeep: A host rots 2%% a minute and slows below half; at 0 it falls apart. Embalming Fluid makes it fresh and halves the rot for a day (20 minutes). Neural Lace, used at 50%% sync or more, stops it for good.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.body_l: Use it to store the nearest host within 3 blocks, frozen: nothing rots inside. Use it again to let it out in front. It takes robot shells and your own mecha too.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.robots:
Set a chassis down and use it as a jar to climb in. Shells never rot, are always synced and run on your jar's charge, 3 FE/t.
• Lunk: strong; tosses things
• Rover: fast, sprints; 9-slot hold
• Spider Walker: climbs, spins webs
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.person: The first time the company touches a creature (a sample, a cut, a head set down or fitted) it gets a staff number and a Personnel File. Old heads and hosts are filed as they turn up.

Jade shows anyone the number, department and employer; the name only to the employer and those they trust.

We do not lose staff. We occasionally misplace them.

%1$s and use a placed head with an empty hand: its file card opens, with its wage, jar, genes and last eight lines of history.

The employer, or anyone they trust, may rename it there.

Names take 16 characters; a blank keeps the old one. A staff name is not a name tag: the saw does not mind it.

Departments go by species: cows are Livestock, creepers Demolitions. Shells are Temp Agency.

A head at a Cerebral Array sits on the Board while it is there.

A wild creature has a file but no employer. Nobody is told when it goes.

When a host that worked for someone dies, its employer gets an Exit Interview in chat, and this drops where it fell.

Your own file is also on file.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.1: A placed head is a trophy until someone hires it: by paying its wage by hand (wheat for a cow, two rotten flesh for a zombie) or by giving it lunch. Whoever does is its employer.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.2:
Staff wear a badge in the employer's team colour, company teal without one.

At each dawn a head on the payroll takes one wage from a chest, barrel or other container touching it.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.3:
A head left unloaded for a week takes one wage, not seven. A trophy never touches the chest beside it.

Paying by hand twice in a day does nothing: it was paid today.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.4:
Starts at 50: +10 a wage paid, -15 a dawn unpaid.
Engaged, 75-100: chin up
Content, 40-74
Disengaged, 15-39: sags, looks away
Grievance: under 15 two dawns running. A label, for now.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.5:
Heads at stations show Content.
An Employee Mount's villager, by its pay: today and yesterday, Engaged; today, Content; unpaid 1-2 days, Disengaged; 3 or more, Grievance.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.6: A villager head is never paid by hand: an emerald in hand opens its trades, as it always has. Lunch hires it, and slimes, ghasts, tadpoles and the others that draw no wage.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.7:
At dawn, on lunch: fed, +5 (up to 60); hungry, -5 (down to 30).
Colleague of its department within 8: +2. Rival within 4: -5. A dislike: -5.
Any time: cake, +40, once a day; sampled, -10.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.8: Dislikes: panda, thunder; bee, enderman, rain; polar bear, heat; zombie, drowned, zombie villager, skeleton, phantom, open sky; blaze, rain, water; strider, outside the Nether; snow golem, warmth, rain; hoglin, warped fungus.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.pay.9:
Rivals: villager and zombie villager, pillager or vindicator; skeleton and wolf; piglin and wither skeleton; creeper and cat or ocelot; spider and armadillo.

A pizza party is not a pay rise.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.1:
Every placed head has a title: the cow is the Canteen Supervisor.

Use one with an empty hand: the bell rings, it nods and says something. HR translates.

Fed, it does its desk job.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.2: Lunch: use the bucket on the plinth. The bowl holds 1,000 mB, three days of lunch. A cow head within 8 makes it last 10%% longer. The first lunch hires a trophy; then pipes may feed it too.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.3:
Desk Jobs
Items are used on the head, fed.
Villager: rung with an emerald in hand, reads its best offer.
Cow: broth near it lasts longer.
Sheep: shears, wool daily; dye, a new colour.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.4:
Mooshroom: a bowl, stew daily; a brown one fed a flower, suspicious stew.
Chicken: clucks the hour; a feather at dawn.
Blaze: furnaces it touches cook 25%% faster.
Evoker: turns a blue sheep within 8 red.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.5:
Cat: creepers keep 6 blocks off, phantoms 16; a dawn gift if its employer slept.
Ghast: a tear at dawn; a wail at night.
Frog: croaks a minute before rain.
Squid: a glass bottle, an ink sac daily.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.6:
Piglin: a gold ingot, one barter. Off a Nether block, out of the Nether, it turns in 15 s.
Allay: use an item on it: every 30 s it fetches one like it within 16 into a chest it touches.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.7:
Goat: rung, rams its glass: a horn, twice ever.
Sniffer: on dirt, grass, moss or mud, a seed at dawn.
Iron Golem: villager heads within 16 cheer up; a poppy on the first ring of the day.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.8:
Zombie: knocks on a door when someone comes near.
Warden: logs every sound within 16; rung, reads out the last five. Over 20 a minute: -5 morale. At Grievance, one shriek: Darkness, 10 s, within 16.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.desk.9:
Morale sets the pace: Engaged, a fifth faster; Disengaged, half speed, and it complains every two minutes. A Disengaged ghast cries two tears.

A head taken off its plinth says goodbye. It leaves the stapler.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.treadm: Two blocks long. Ride a host onto the belt and get off with %1$s: "Clocked in." It walks in place: 4 to 24 FE/t by species (a cow 10, a camel 24, anything unlisted 8).

It holds 10 kFE and pushes up to 1,000 FE/t from its near end into touching machines, as the Galvanic Pile does. A body on the belt rots twice as fast (embalmed: at the usual rate). A laced body is Tired: half output, forever. Full sync: +10%%.

Ridden, it makes power too, and forward goes nowhere. Use it with an empty hand to read it. Fliers, swimmers, ghasts, striders, slimes, shells and the heavy ones (golems, ravagers, wardens, hoglins) refuse.

A healthy body is a productive body.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.lookou: Any head takes a Turret Pedestal. The thirteen that fight still fight. Any other is a Lookout: a hostile within 16, in sight, and it raises its species' alarm every 5 s and makes the hostile glow. 1 FE/t, 2 alarmed.

A comparator on the pedestal reads 15 while it is alarmed, or while a fighting head has a target, and 2 s after.

Wire it to a redstone lamp: the cow lights the hall.

Cow heads do not bite. That is not the point.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.every_:
Every vanilla body does something at 50%% sync:
Moo: cow
Rooting: pig
Shed: sheep
Spit: llama
Sound the Bell: villager
Barter: piglin (a gold ingot)

Warm Up: strider, on lava
Withdraw: turtle
Long Jump: frog
Hiss: cat

At 75%%:
Dash: camel
Rear: horse, donkey, mule

Mend: iron golem (an iron ingot)
Howl: wolf
Treasure Sense: dolphin

Gold and iron come from your pockets.

Traits at 25%%: a sheep takes half fall damage; iron golems leave a villager alone, piglins a piglin. A strider walks on lava and a cat keeps phantoms off, as they always have.

A chicken sawn without a jar runs in circles where it was cut, never more than 12 blocks out.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.workfo: Use a Staff Lanyard on a living creature to hire it. It stops, looks at you and stands awaiting assignment until a Time Clock of yours within 16 blocks takes it.

Its own mind is off: it never despawns, attacks nobody and works for you with its temperament kept as a quirk.

Hostiles first need wearing down to half their health. Babies, bosses, hosts, creepers, fish, bats, vexes and shulkers are not hired.

Someone else's pet or staff, and a village's iron golem, are not yours to poach. A golem you built is.

A player employs 24 at most; a clock takes 8.
Let go: %1$s and use a Clipboard on it, twice within 3 seconds. The lanyard comes back with a Form 45-S (and the Hard Hat). It serves 10 seconds' notice, head down, then it is a creature again.

A Security colleague sees it out. A hostile is hostile again once the notice is up.

Turret Pedestals, iron golems and wolves spare staff, unless staff start it.

Wear your badge at all times. It is how we know you are staff.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.time_c: A Time Clock makes a site: 16 blocks out on the level, 8 up and 8 down. Clocks need 8 blocks between them. Use it for the Roster, the Job Rack, the Pay Drawer and the Shifts.
At each shift staff walk up, punch in one at a time, take a card and go. Off shift they stand in a line by the clock, facing it. The late get the bell.

Day: 1,000 to 11,000
Night: 13,000 to 23,000
Redstone: while the clock is powered

Times are the Overworld's everywhere. Undead start on Night; Day needs a Hard Hat.

At dawn each worker takes its wage from the Pay Drawer, as a plinth head does from its chest. A hopper may fill the drawer; nothing takes from it but staff.

Untrusted players are refused at the clock.

Undead within 2 blocks of their own clock do not burn: the clock has an awning.

A broken clock drops its drawer and rack; its staff wait for another clock within 16 blocks.

Punch in. Punch out. Punch nothing else.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.job_ca: Use a Clipboard on your clock to bind it. Use a container in the site: a Pick-Up. %1$s and use one: a Drop-Off. Use two other blocks: the corners of an area.
Use it in the air: choose the job, a filter for each Drop-Off, a name, and Print: one paper becomes a Job Card. Put cards in the Job Rack, or give one to a worker by hand.

Idle staff take the first card they can do with the fewest workers on it: one card, eight workers; eight cards, one each.

Fields and pens are at most 16 by 16.

Hauling: Pick-Up to Drop-Off
Sorting: one Pick-Up, by filter
Farming: ripe crops, replanted; sheep and cows in a pen
Security: patrols, sees hostiles off the site

Each kind has its aptitudes: zombies cannot read the labels, cats have one job, fliers fly. Disengaged staff misfile one item in twenty. Nobody tramples, breaks a block or leaves the site.

A Job Card is a promise. Staff keep promises. Mostly.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.hard_h: Use it on a worker to put it on. Undead staff in one may work the Day shift and do not burn. Falling blocks do staff no harm. It never wears out.

Only a Hard Hat counts: Policy 4.1, hard hats, not helmets.

You may wear one too: a leather helmet's armour, and half the harm from falling blocks. It fits a Hat Mount.

Health and Safety thanks you.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.whistl: Use it on your staff to put them on your detail (six at most). Use it in the air: Follow or Hold. %1$s and use it: they are stood down and go home.

Attack with it in hand: the fighters go for what you point at. Cats, wolves, parrots and foxes are pets: they keep you company instead.

A detail never follows you through a portal.

Left far behind, or five minutes away from you, they take the company shuttle back to their clock. Nothing is loaded to fetch them.

A jar needs a Speaker Grille to whistle.

An away day is still a working day.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.workfo:
Staff think twice a second, each in turn, and never load a chunk: an unloaded site stops like a furnace. Paths stay inside the site.

Operators have /headoffice staff list, recall and pause.
book.headinajar.written2.staffing.second: Use a Secondment Collar on a host, with hands. Then Use a jarred head on it: the jar twists on and the head drives the body. It is staff now, on its own file, and looks for a Time Clock of yours.

The head is skills: its jobs and how fast, its wage, its turret post (an attacking head shoots from the jar), its temper.

The body is hardware: how it moves, hands, carry, health, and its tricks.

Team Sync
1%% every 24 s of work, on shift with a card; half when the blood does not mix (an oil body takes any head).
25%%: the body's traits
50%%: its Ability; the lace takes
75%%: its Secondary
100%%: 10%% faster, carries 10%% more

The collar's canister holds 500 mB: a mB every 6 seconds, about 50 minutes. It tops up at each punch-in from the clock's Broth tank. Dry, the head sags and the body stands by.

The body still rots. A mixed team needs Embalming Fluid before the lace.

When the body dies the collar fires the Redundancy Package: the head floats down under a little gold canopy and lands as a placed head, file and grade kept.

It is lost only if its glass was gone, it fell into the void, or it came down in lava.

Sneak and Use with an empty hand: the head comes off into your hand. Shears take an empty collar back. A Glass Patch mends the jar, a bucket of broth fills the canister, a syringe held sneaking draws the head.

A body with no mind meets a mind with no body. HR calls it synergy.

book.headinajar.written2.research.direct: Open a DNA Sequencer and press the Directory tab: the 82 vanilla creatures by department, each with its spawn egg. A cell is stamped when your team samples the species, jars its head, or rides it as a host. Teammates share one Directory; alone, it is yours.

Point at a cell for its blood, tool, genes and your reads, its title and the jar it needs; a blank cell gives a hint. Three are [REDACTED] until filed. 10 species stamped: a memo. 25 jarred: Headhunter. All 77 species on the books sampled: Complete Census.

book.headinajar.written2.hr.faq.1:
Can I drink the saline? No.

Can a jar sit in the chair? No, but it can look at the panel.

Can my body take a portal? Only carrying its head, or over an Entangled Pair. A jar takes any.
book.headinajar.written2.hr.faq.2:
What if my jar breaks? A real death: modules, goggles and collar drop, and you respawn whole. The jar menu's Let Go button does this on purpose.
Can I saw a colleague? No. Nor bosses, named creatures, others' pets or hosts.
book.headinajar.written2.hr.incidents.1:
Incident 0311: Mecha wrecked

Below 10%% health, the Golden Parachute threw the pilot clear. A frame destroyed outright throws the pilot too, with a knock to the glass; about half its modules survive. Next: a Glass Patch.
book.headinajar.written2.hr.incidents.2:
Incident 0451: Head left in a fire

The glass lost a point a second until it broke: a real death. Next time: fetch it with the Head Satchel at once, or fit a Heat Shield.
book.headinajar.written2.hr.incidents.3:

A body left standing was killed and lay down as a corpse. Next: the Courier, then a Suture Kit. A Life Sign Monitor shows its health.
